report.source_text: Two years after the diagnosis of acquired EPP, our patient was able to control his photosensitivity with the above-mentioned sun-protective measures and did not require the use of afamelanotide. To date, he has not developed any signs of liver toxicity despite consistently high levels of plasma porphyrins, which are being monitored on regular basis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man with a history of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) presented with a 2-year history of sun sensitivity characterized by burning pain, blistering, crusting lesions, and scars on sun-exposed skin. Clinical examination showed thickened, lichenified skin with fresh blister, crusts, scars, and milia on hands, neck, and face. Skin biopsy revealed subepidermal blistering with sparse inflammation, suggestive of porphyria. Biochemical testing demonstrated massively elevated plasma total porphyrins and free protoporphyrin levels, confirming erythropoietic protoporphyria. The diagnosis of acquired EPP secondary to MDS was established. Two years post-diagnosis, the patient managed photosensitivity with sun protection, without need for afamelanotide, and showed no liver toxicity despite persistently high plasma porphyrins.
